protocol: A chain is a true positive (TP) when, in some real execution, the value written to its sink can carry free text from an external HTTP client: for CWE-89 a quote, for CWE-117 a CR or LF (the services log plain text with the default %m pattern, which does not escape them).

The chain's root does not decide the label: a listener-rooted chain whose message field is filled with client text by its producer is a TP, a chain rooted at an endpoint whose field never reaches the sink unvalidated is not.

Reasons of a false positive (FP): VALIDATED - bean validation limits the value to a charset without quotes or line breaks; NON_TEXT - number, enum, UUID or an id generated by the server; SERVER_TEXT - a string a trusted service builds itself; INFEASIBLE - the path cannot execute (the analysis is path-insensitive or merges exception objects).
Rules are tried in order and the first one whose patterns all match labels the chain. A chain no rule matches is an error, so that every new chain is labelled consciously.
